reason: Attacked on the one soft spot the evidence leaves and it held. The evidence names Project Gutenberg 18269, whose own front matter credits only T. S. Eliot for the introduction and names no translator: it is the Dutton paperback of 1958. So the file that was read does not itself say Trotter, and the source line dates the translation 1910, which is neither the file read nor, on its face, an edition anyone had opened. I closed that gap rather than trusting it. I downloaded the OCR of archive.org item thoughtstrbywftr00pascuoft, whose title page reads Thoughts, tr. by W. F. Trotter, P. F. Collier and Son, copyright 1910, the Harvard Classics printing. Its contents list Of the Means of Belief as the fourth section, and at fragment 282 it prints: We know truth, not only by the reason, but also by the heart, and it is in this last way that we know first principles; and reason, which has no part in it, tries in vain to impugn them. Word for word and comma for comma the proposed line, in a printing of the named translation dated by the year the source gives. So trans. W. F. Trotter, 1910 is a true and locatable citation, not a guess. The Gutenberg file is independently confirmed as Trotter by its rendering of fragment 277, The heart has its reasons, which reason does not know, which is Trotter's signature line. Section IV headed OF THE MEANS OF BELIEF and the Brunschvicg number 282 both check out in both printings. Attribution: Pascal's own, not a character, no trap in the brief's misattribution list applies. shipped.js returns no exact match, no near match, blaise pascal at 1 of 3 for the year from March, not banned. Scope: philosophy, first published 1670, well before 1999, no scripture, no oratory, nothing needing a warning. Form checks: the source line is 96 characters, leads with the name, no em dash; the quotation ends in a full stop and holds no straight double quote; the tag Philosophy is the form of the work. One flag for the editor, not a refutation: the note is empty, and it would be worth a line saying the wording was checked against the 1910 Collier printing, since the Dutton reprint named in the evidence does not name its translator.
